The **51st G7 summit** , the 57th annual meeting of the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7 "G7"), was held from 16 to 17 June 2025 in [Kananaskis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kananaskis_Improvement_District "Kananaskis Improvement District"), Alberta, Canada.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-2) This was the 2nd G7 summit to be held in Kananaskis since the [28th G8 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28th_G8_summit "28th G8 summit") in 2002,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-4) and the seventh summit held in Canada. The 2025 summit therefore makes Kananaskis the first Canadian village to host a G7 or G8 leaders' summit twice.
## Leaders at the summit
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=51st_G7_summit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Leaders at the summit")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/2025-11-14_InaugurationREM_Deux-Montagnes_Mark_Carney.jpg/250px-2025-11-14_InaugurationREM_Deux-Montagnes_Mark_Carney.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2025-11-14_InaugurationREM_Deux-Montagnes_Mark_Carney.jpg)[Mark Carney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Carney "Mark Carney") chaired the 51st G7 summit. [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/51st_G7_Summit_Family_photo.jpg/250px-51st_G7_Summit_Family_photo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:51st_G7_Summit_Family_photo.jpg)G7 leaders with the leaders of invited countries
The 2025 summit was the first summit for European Council President [António Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa "António Costa"), British prime minister [Keir Starmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer"), Canadian prime minister [Mark Carney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Carney "Mark Carney"), and German chancellor [Friedrich Merz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Merz "Friedrich Merz"). It was also the first and only summit for Japanese prime minister [Shigeru Ishiba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeru_Ishiba "Shigeru Ishiba"). The visit marked the first international visit to Canada for British prime minister [Keir Starmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer"), Japanese prime minister [Shigeru Ishiba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeru_Ishiba "Shigeru Ishiba"), German chancellor [Friedrich Merz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Merz "Friedrich Merz"), Australian prime minister [Anthony Albanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Albanese "Anthony Albanese"), South Korean president [Lee Jae Myung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jae_Myung "Lee Jae Myung"), and marked the second visit to Canada by Italian prime minister [Giorgia Meloni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgia_Meloni "Giorgia Meloni") and US president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and the first visit since the [44th G7 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_G7_summit "44th G7 summit") in 2018. It marked the third visit to Canada for French president [Emmanuel Macron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Macron "Emmanuel Macron") and Ukrainian president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy").
In May, Mexican president [Claudia Sheinbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_Sheinbaum "Claudia Sheinbaum") was invited to attend.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-5) Following the announcement, she told reporters that she had not decided if she would attend, but that it is "a possibility".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-Agren1-7) On 30 May, Brazilian president [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva") was invited and is expected to attend.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-Soares1-8) In June, Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia [Mohammed bin Salman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_bin_Salman "Mohammed bin Salman") was invited. However, on 12 June it was confirmed that he will not be attending the summit.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-MBSInviteDecline-10)
Indonesian president [Prabowo Subianto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabowo_Subianto "Prabowo Subianto") was initially invited by Mark Carney to attend the G7 summit,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-11) which he accepted.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-12) However, on 12 June, Prabowo announced that he would skip the summit and meet Singaporean prime minister [Lawrence Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Wong "Lawrence Wong"), Vietnamese president [Lương Cường](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C6%B0%C6%A1ng_C%C6%B0%E1%BB%9Dng "Lương Cường"), and Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") instead.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-15)

### Foreign Ministers' Meeting (12–14 March)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=51st_G7_summit&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Foreign Ministers' Meeting \(12–14 March\)")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Secretary_Rubio_Participates_in_G7_Meeting_on_Strengthening_the_G7_%2854384404933%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Rubio_Participates_in_G7_Meeting_on_Strengthening_the_G7_%2854384404933%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Rubio_Participates_in_G7_Meeting_on_Strengthening_the_G7_\(54384404933\).jpg)G7 Foreign Ministers meeting in Charlevoix, 13 March 2025
During the G7 Foreign Ministers meeting in Charlevoix on 12–14 March 2025 they made agreements on the following issues:[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-25)
  * Ukraine's long-term prosperity and security
  * Regional peace and stability in the Middle East
  * Cooperation to increase security and resilience across the Indo-Pacific
  * Building stability and resilience in Haiti and Venezuela
  * Supporting lasting peace in Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  * Strengthening sanctions and countering hybrid warfare and sabotage


## Events leading to the summit
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=51st_G7_summit&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Events leading to the summit")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Prime_Minister_Keir_Starmer_meets_Canada%27s_Mark_Carney_%2854591804295%29.jpg/250px-Prime_Minister_Keir_Starmer_meets_Canada%27s_Mark_Carney_%2854591804295%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Prime_Minister_Keir_Starmer_meets_Canada's_Mark_Carney_\(54591804295\).jpg)Canadian Prime Minister [Mark Carney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Carney "Mark Carney") with British Prime Minister [Keir Starmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer") at Parliament Hill, Ottawa, 15 June 2025 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Participation_of_Ursula_von_der_Leyen%2C_President_of_the_European_Commission%2C_to_the_G7_Summit.jpg/250px-Participation_of_Ursula_von_der_Leyen%2C_President_of_the_European_Commission%2C_to_the_G7_Summit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Participation_of_Ursula_von_der_Leyen,_President_of_the_European_Commission,_to_the_G7_Summit.jpg)Working session on 16 June 2025
On 14 June, Canadian prime minister Carney and British prime minister Starmer held their bilateral meeting in [Ottawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa "Ottawa"). On route to Ottawa, Starmer stated that "Canada is an independent, sovereign country and a much-valued [member of the Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Commonwealth_of_Nations "Member states of the Commonwealth of Nations")" in the wake of President Trump's threats to [annex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movements_for_the_annexation_of_Canada_to_the_United_States "Movements for the annexation of Canada to the United States") Canada as the [51st state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state "51st state").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-26) Upon arrival, Starmer had dinner with Canadian prime minister [Mark Carney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Carney "Mark Carney") at his official residence at [Rideau Cottage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rideau_Cottage "Rideau Cottage"), later the two watched a [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Stanley_Cup_Final "2025 Stanley Cup Final") game between the [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers") and [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panthers "Florida Panthers").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-27) They agreed to establish an Economic and Trade Working Group and to deepen the [Trade Continuity Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_Kingdom_Trade_Continuity_Agreement "Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement"), while Carney committed Canada to ratifying the UK's [accession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accession_of_the_United_Kingdom_to_CPTPP "Accession of the United Kingdom to CPTPP") to [CPTPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_and_Progressive_Agreement_for_Trans-Pacific_Partnership "Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-30) The meeting was the first between two international leaders since Israel's [strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_2025_Israeli_strikes_on_Iran "June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran") on Iran starting the [2025 Iran–Israel conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Iran%E2%80%93Israel_conflict "2025 Iran–Israel conflict"); Starmer began a diplomatic push to try to de-escalate the [Middle Eastern crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Eastern_crisis_\(2023%E2%80%93present\) "Middle Eastern crisis \(2023–present\)").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-32)

## Twelve-Day War
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=51st_G7_summit&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Twelve-Day War")]
Following the outbreak of the [Twelve-Day War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve-Day_War "Twelve-Day War"), Trump stated that he needed to leave to control the United States's response to the conflict, which meant that he sidelined some scheduled meetings with world leaders.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-33)
On 16 June 2025, G7 leaders said: "We affirm that Israel has a right to defend itself. We reiterate our support for the security of Israel. Iran is the principal source of regional instability and terror."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-34)
## Post summit
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=51st_G7_summit&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Post summit")]
From 11 to 12 November 2025, the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting was held at [Niagara-on-the-Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niagara-on-the-Lake "Niagara-on-the-Lake"), and joint statement was issued.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-35) The joint statement showed their consensus on Ukraine and Sudan, but stayed away from contentious issues like the US military strikes on boats in the Caribbean and trade. They are increasing the economic costs to Russia and exploring measures against those who finance Russia's war efforts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-36) Also, they raised alarm over China's military buildup and reiterated their resolve to create an alternative to its dominance in critical mineral supplies, and reaffirmed the importance of a [Free and Open Indo-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_Open_Indo-Pacific "Free and Open Indo-Pacific") based on the [rule of law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_law "Rule of law").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_G7_summit#cite_note-37)
